Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From a808a04c861782e31fc30e342a619c144aaee14a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nathan Chancellor <natechancellor@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Dec 2019 18:47:26 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: csiostor: Adjust indentation in csio_device_reset

Clang warns:

../drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c:1386:3: warning: misleading
indentation; statement is not part of the previous 'if'
[-Wmisleading-indentation]
         csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
         ^
../drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c:1382:2: note: previous statement is
here
        if (*buf != '1')
        ^
1 warning generated.

This warning occurs because there is a space after the tab on this
line.  Remove it so that the indentation is consistent with the Linux
kernel coding style and clang no longer warns.

Fixes: a3667aaed569 ("[SCSI] csiostor: Chelsio FCoE offload driver")
Link: https://github.com/ClangBuiltLinux/linux/issues/818
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20191218014726.8455-1-natechancellor@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Nathan Chancellor <natechancellor@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c b/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
index 469d0bc9f5fe..00cf33573136 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c
@@ -1383,7 +1383,7 @@ csio_device_reset(struct device *dev,
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	/* Delete NPIV lnodes */
-	 csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
+	csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);
 
 	/* Block upper IOs */
 	csio_lnodes_block_request(hw);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/scsi/csiostor/csio_scsi.c`**
- The line ` csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` had an extra space before it, which caused misleading indentation warnings from Clang.
- The modification removed the leading space, changing it to `csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` to ensure consistent indentation according to the Linux kernel coding style.

### Relationships
- The change addresses a specific warning generated by Clang regarding misleading indentation, which can lead to confusion about the control flow of the code. 
- The fix is linked to a previous commit identified by the hash `a3667aaed569`, which introduced the code that is now being corrected for style compliance. 
- The patch is part of an ongoing effort to maintain code quality and adherence to coding standards within the Linux kernel, as indicated by the links provided in the patch description.

This can lead to confusion about the control flow, potentially causing the function to behave incorrectly if developers misinterpret the intended logic.

Removing the extra space before `csio_lnodes_exit(hw, 1);` aligns it correctly with the `if` statement, ensuring that it is recognized as part of the conditional block. This adjustment clarifies the control flow and adheres to the Linux kernel coding style, eliminating the warning from Clang.
